catalog_quote: Stress is dynamic and similar to that in dari (Afghan) Persian (see Farhadi, 1975, pp. 64-67) and tājiki (Rastorgueva, pp. 9-10) Persian, and not variable (as suggested by Dulling, p. 37). It generally falls on the last syllable of a nominal form, including derivative suffixes and a number of morphological markers. ... Particles, conjunctions, modals, and adverbials. These include atê / arê “yes”; ammo, liken, wali “but”; balki “however”; šayti “perhaps”; bayti “it is necessary”; i(n)ji “here,” ûnji “there”; oli “now,” wuḵt-a “then.” These are also marked by distinctive initial stress. Verb morphology. The imperfective marker is mi- (assimilated variants m-, mu-, m-, mê-), e.g., mi-zan-um “I hit, I am hitting”; the subjunctive and imperative marker is bi- (with similar assimilation); the negation is na-, e.g., na-mi-zad-um “I was not hitting.” These usually attract stress.

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding quotation is verbatim in the held the Internet Archive text of Kieffer's EIr article, at the three named sections. (2) The classification rested on a 2003 encyclopedia sketch that is avowedly second-hand on Efimov. I downloaded the primary source it summarizes (Efimov 1997, Jazyki mira, open PDF at ILing RAN, scanned sec. 2.1.2, book p. 157): dynamic bound stress, usually on the last syllable; adverbs/modals/particles non-final (ínji, óli, šáyti); in verbs with the formative prefixes (mi-, bi-, na-) main stress on the prefix with secondary stress on the personal ending; in unprefixed verb forms stress placement 'not strictly fixed' (ámadum ~ amádum ~ amadúm). sources.quote: 'Ударение динамическое, связанное. Обычно падает на последний слог: [qučqár 'ram', kitób 'book', kitobó 'books']. В наречиях, модальных и [союзных] словах ударение падает не на последний слог: [ínji 'here', óli 'now', šáyti 'perhaps']. В глаголах с формообразующими приставками (см. 2.1.3.) основное ударение падает на первый слог, т. е. на приставку, а добавочное — на личное окончание: mé-madum 'я приходил'. В глагольных формах, образуемых без указанных приставок, место ударения строго не закреплено: ámadum/amádum/amadúm 'я пришел'.' Plus 2.1.4: stress may occasionally shift onto an epenthetic

sources.note: A general monograph on the Hazaragi dialect ('roots and features'); Glottolog types it 'comparative' (origins/affiliation), so a chapter on phonetic features is plausible but unverified. Hazaragi is an Eastern Persian variety with Dari/Tajik-type dynamic word-final stress (Efimov 1997, Kieffer 2003, a work listed here); no source treats it as tonal, so any prosodic content here would be a stress statement, not a tone inventory.
